author: ramanuja
summary: An independent prose treatise in which Ramanuja sets out how the Upanishads, read as a whole, teach Vishishtadvaita.
whyRead: Shorter and more direct than the Sri Bhashya, it is a good place to see Ramanuja's central interpretive move: reconciling Upanishadic statements of difference and of non-difference through the body-soul relationship.
questions: How can scripture teach both unity and difference?
What is the meaning of the Upanishads as a whole?

keyTeachings.title: Reconciling unity and difference
keyTeachings.text: Some Upanishadic passages stress difference between God and souls, others identity; Ramanuja reads both through passages that describe God as the inner self of all.

keyTeachings.title: Critique of rival readings
keyTeachings.text: He critiques Advaita and the Bhedabheda (difference-in-identity) views of earlier Vedantins.
